Take the lead in operations at Skechers and guide your teams toward excellence in a fully automated and fast-growing environment!

Skechers USA is a global leader in lifestyle and performance footwear, generating $9 billion in annual revenue. The company designs, develops, and markets over 3,000 styles for men, women, and children.

Why join Skechers?

• A fast-growing international company
• A warm, dynamic, and tech-forward work environment
• A culture that embraces diversity and inclusion
• A competitive salary package
• The extra perk? An on-site gym with a personal coach
To strengthen its operational team, our client Skechers is currently looking for an Operations Manager for its site in Herstal.

 

 

Jobomschrijving

As an Operations Manager at Skechers, you report directly to the Director of Operations and independently manage several departments.

Your key responsibilities include:

• Planning, organizing, and supervising daily operations to meet short- and long-term goals, while ensuring budget, deadlines, and safety standards are met in an automated environment.
• Promoting and maintaining a strong safety culture.
• Developing strategic business plans for the short, medium, and long term for your departments.

• Managing and optimizing automated processes with a continuous improvement mindset.
This role requires adaptability, versatility, and a proactive approach to overcoming daily challenges and driving operational excellence.

Education and technical skills:

• Minimum 3 years of proven experience in a similar role within an automated/production environment.
• Proficiency in WMS, WCS, and AS400 systems.
• Solid knowledge of Microsoft Office tools (Excel, Word, Outlook).
• Strong working knowledge of English.
Your personality and soft skills:

• Leadership – You are a driver of change and adapt easily to a constantly evolving environment.
• Communication – You adjust your communication to suit your audience and actively listen.

jobs.description:
Are you looking to build your career as a Junior Controller in an international industrial environment? A growing manufacturing company based in Brussels is looking for a motivated finance professional to strengthen its controlling team.

 

As a Junior Controller, you will gain valuable exposure to industrial finance, production costs and business performance. Whether you have started your career in audit or controlling, this Junior Financial Controller opportunity offers the chance to develop your analytical skills, work closely with operational teams and contribute to important financial decisions.

What you'll do as a junior controller : 

As a Junior Controller, you will work alongside experienced finance professionals and support the company's financial performance through a variety of responsibilities.

• Analyse monthly financial results and investigate variances between actual performance, budgets and forecasts.
• Monitor production costs, operating expenses and profit margins to support effective cost control.
• Prepare financial reports and management dashboards to provide clear insights into business performance.
• Support monthly closing activities and ensure the accuracy of financial information.
• Contribute to budgeting and forecasting processes in collaboration with the finance and operations teams.
• Identify cost optimisation opportunities and investigate the financial drivers behind production performance.
• Develop and improve Excel reports and financial analysis tools.
• Assist the Senior Controller with ad hoc analyses, reporting improvements and business projects.

What we're Looking For as a Junior Controller : 

• A Bachelor's or Master's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics or a related field.
• A first professional experience in audit, financial controlling.
• A genuine interest in industrial controlling, cost accounting and financial performance analysis.
• Strong analytical skills, attention to detail and a structured approach to problem solving.
• Good knowledge of Excel. Experience with SAP or another ERP system is an advantage.
• The ability to communicate financial information clearly and collaborate with non-financial stakeholders.
• Professional proficiency in English, French and a good command of Dutch.

Compliance • Conformity • Governance • Operational Readiness • License to Operate
  
 
  
PMO-C²Trust — Turning Compliance and Conformity into Operational Readiness.
  
Are you an experienced Project Manager who thrives in complex industrial environments where engineering, compliance, safety, permitting and operational readiness converge? Do you enjoy bringing structure to multidisciplinary projects and helping clients navigate regulatory and conformity requirements with confidence? Then the role of PMO-C²Trust Project Manager could be your next challenge.
  
 
  
About PMO-C²Trust: PMO-C²Trust is Kiwa Vinçotte's governance framework for complex industrial investment and engineering projects. Our mission is to help clients translate compliance, conformity and operational requirements into a structured, traceable and manageable project approach that supports a successful License to Operate. We connect project objectives, regulatory obligations, engineering activities, stakeholder responsibilities, conformity requirements and commissioning readiness into one integrated governance model. By creating visibility, accountability and evidence throughout the project lifecycle, we help clients reduce risk, avoid late surprises and achieve safe and compliant project delivery.
  
 
  
Your Mission: as a PMO-C²Trust Project Manager, you guide industrial projects from early project definition through engineering, construction, commissioning and operational release. You ensure that compliance, conformity, safety and permitting requirements are identified at an early stage, translated into practical project actions and managed through to successful completion. You act as a trusted governance partner for clients and create alignment between asset owners, engineering teams, suppliers, contractors, inspection bodies and certification organisations. Your work contributes directly to safe start-up, operational readiness and long-term compliance.
  
 
  
Your Responsibilities:
  
 
  
Compliance & Conformity Management
    
• Identify and assess applicable European, national and regional legislation.  
• Develop compliance and conformity roadmaps for industrial projects.  
• Translate requirements related to CE Marking, the EU Blue Guide and regulatory frameworks into clear project deliverables.  
• Coordinate interfaces with inspection bodies, notified bodies, certification organisations and authorities.  
• Support clients in managing compliance risks throughout the project lifecycle.   
Project Governance & Stakeholder Management
    
• Establish project governance structures, reporting lines and decision-making processes.  
• Facilitate stakeholder alignment across clients, engineering teams, contractors and suppliers.  
• Define responsibilities, interfaces and escalation paths.  
• Support steering committees, reviews and key project decision points.   
Operational Readiness & License to Operate
    
• Integrate conformity, safety, environmental and commissioning requirements into project execution.  
• Coordinate the collection and management of required evidence and project documentation.  
• Monitor project readiness, compliance status and key risks.  
• Support evidence-based decisions for commissioning, handover and ...

Education & Experience
    
• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Engineering, Technology or another relevant technical discipline.  
• Minimum 5 years of experience in industrial, engineering, infrastructure, energy or manufacturing projects.  
• Proven experience in multidisciplinary project management.  
• Experience with industrial commissioning, conformity assessment, compliance management or operational readiness programmes is a strong asset.  
• Project Management certification (PMP, IPMA, PRINCE2 or equivalent) is considered a plus.   
Knowledge & Affinity
  
You have experience or affinity with several of the following domains:
    
• European product legislation and conformity assessment;  
• CE Marking and EU Blue Guide principles;  
• EU New Legislative Framework (NLF);  
• Industrial commissioning and operational readiness;  
• Environmental permitting and compliance requirements;  
• Occupational safety and statutory inspections;  
• Governance, stakeholder management and stage-gate methodologies.   
Knowledge of Belgian and Flemish environmental legislation, including VLAREM, is a strong asset.
  
Your strength lies in connecting expertise, asking the right questions and translating complex requirements into a coherent project approach.
  
 
  
Competencies
  
You:
    
• Translate complexity into structure and action.  
• Are comfortable working with both technical specialists and senior stakeholders.  
• Proactively identify risks, gaps and opportunities.  
• Combine ownership with strong organisational skills.  
• Balance regulatory rigour with practical project delivery.  
• Build trust through a professional, solution-oriented approach.   
Languages
    
• Dutch: Fluent  
• English: Professional proficiency  
• French: Strong asset   
You are willing to travel within Belgium and occasionally across Europe.

Your mandate: execution, ownership and results 
You will personally lead the on-site execution of a major industrial project while overseeing several others, with individual projects worth several million euros. Your responsibility extends from site mobilisation and execution through handover and contractual and financial close-out.
 
This is neither a design-engineering position nor a remote project oversight role. You will be close to the work, teams, subcontractors and customers — while maintaining control of safety, quality, deadlines, budgets, margins and contractual commitments.
 Where you will make the difference  
• Deliver on site. Set execution priorities, coordinate multidisciplinary teams and subcontractors, resolve operational issues and ensure safe, high-quality delivery. 
• Protect project performance. Own budgets, forecasts, costs, cash flow and margins; spot deviations early and act before they affect results. 
• Manage contractual complexity. Anticipate risks, handle variations and claims, contribute to negotiations and safeguard customer relationships, including in public-sector projects. 
• Lead and develop people. Guide a team of approximately five to six project professionals, building accountability, confidence and stronger project practices. 
• Create clarity. Use practical planning, reporting and project reviews to turn complex situations into timely decisions — without unnecessary bureaucracy. 
 
• At least 7 years managing complex industrial projects, including substantial, hands-on responsibility for on-site execution. 
• At least 3 years in project management roles, with proven ability to lead and develop multidisciplinary teams. 
• Strong financial and contractual judgement: budgets, margins, forecasts, risk, negotiation and claims. 
• A sound technical foundation, ideally in mechanical, electromechanical, civil or industrial engineering; other educational backgrounds are welcome with substantial relevant experience. 
•  Fluent French and English; basic Dutch is an advantage. Experience with public procurement is particularly valuable.  
Above all, you enjoy the reality of industrial sites. You are pragmatic, structured and decisive; you can challenge technical choices, understand their commercial consequences and bring people with you.
